### Research

**Cornell College**

**Building Text Analysis Tools for Scottish Gaelic** *(Nov 2023 – Present)*

- Collaborative project with Dr. Pete Barclay and Dr. Alistair Lawson at Napier University in Edinburgh, Scotland.
- Building a text corpus of Scottish Gaelic
- Creating Python tools to support text analysis with Scottish Gaelic

**Central Michigan University**

**PhD Dissertation Research** (Advisors: D. Wang and M. Amezziane) *(Jan 2016 – Present)*

- Created two new linear regression lack of fit tests specialized in detecting an array of departures from linearity
- Use power simulations and non-central distribution approximations to find the statistical power of the tests
- Worked on developing an R programming package LOFnorep containing partition lack of fit methods

**Data Analytics Class Project** (Professor: C. Lee) *(Jan 2017 – May 2017)*

- Found and cleaned data containing every documented crime in New York City, New York, recorded via a New York State database
- Unsupervised techniques were used to study the relationship between the number of crimes, the types of crimes, and demographics by geographic location within the city (down to census tract)
- Various predictive models, including linear regression, logistic regression, and neural networks, were fit using cross-validation
- The chosen model was then scored with the most recent crime data, and the model showed that such predictions can be made with the few demographic variables chosen and location

**Graduate Research** (Advisor: D. Wang) *(Jan 2016 – July 2016)*

- Programmed linear regression lack of fit tests into R to make them accessible to more statisticians and simulated new and past results
- Hypothesized application of recommended alterations for sinusoidal data structures

### Courses at Cornell College

**Statistical Methods I** *(Fifteen sections)*

- Taught in hybrid, synchronous online, and asynchronous online formats
- Utilized technologies include learning management system Moodle, Citrix virtual machines, Google Drive, Panopto, Zoom, Google Survey, and an iPad for live annotations of course notes
- Used statistical software Minitab® and StatKey
- Covered topics including data collection, organizing and summarizing data, numerically summarizing data, describing the relation between two variables, sampling distributions, hypothesis testing, and confidence intervals using both theoretical and simulation methods, and linear regression – chapters 1-6 in *Statistics: Unlocking the Power of Data*, 2e by Lock et. al. (2017)
- Used the WileyPlus website corresponding to the above textbook for homework and the eBook

**The History of Statistics in the UK and Ireland** *(One section)*

- Developed the course based on a similar course at the University of Florida
- Course website at: <https://stats-tgeorge.quarto.pub/history-of-stats-uk-ireland/>
- Led students across the British Isles in 22 days to learn about statistics, where they were developed
- Organized logistics, including accommodations, ground transportation, tickets, tours, and some meals
- Talks about this course are available at: <https://github.com/stats-tgeorge/STA257_talks/>

**Second Year Seminar, Community Engaged Statistics** *(Two sections)*

- Bi-annual redevelopment of the course based on the community partner, Waypoint Services, needs.
- Recent course website developed at: <https://stats-tgeorge.github.io/STA200_S4E>
- Coordinated with nonprofits Waypoint Services and Iowa Legal Aid to: agree on reasonable research questions based on data availability and stakeholder interest, gain access to their databases, set up Zoom trainings for partners to teach my students how to access, navigate, and collect data from various sources, including Wellsky, Iowa Courts Online, and EMDS
- Final student presentations included brochures and infographics presented to both the Cornell College community and the community partner Waypoint Services
- Topics included: inequities along race and gender lines, specifically in relation to housing and incarceration, the descriptive statistics to explore, visualize, and understand data, and communicating statistical results to the community partner, including their CEO.
- In the 2023 iteration, co-organized a panel of speakers from five nonprofits in Iowa that serve the unhoused, and a panel of currently and previously unhoused youth from Des Moines, Iowa
- Technologies include Minitab® statistical software and Canva

**Statistical Learning** *(One section)*

- Developed course
- Course website at: <https://sta362-sb8-24.github.io/STA362StatLearning/>
- Topics included cross-validation, model comparison, and fitting, prediction, and interpretation of models, including least squares regression, principal component analysis, decision trees, random forests, boosted trees, K-nearest neighbors, linear and quadratic discriminant analysis, naïve Bayes, and more
- Technologies included R, RStudio, LMS Moodle, Google Drive, Panopto, and Zoom

**Statistics and Data Science Internship Advisor**

- The student collaborated with Cornell admissions to develop an aggregate engagement score, build a logistic regression model to predict whether an individual would attend Cornell, and identify factors related to whether a student would apply and ultimately attend Cornell.
- The student collaborated with the baseball coach to collect data and model, using logistic regression, the optimal pitch styles for inducing strikeouts based on previous pitches.
- The student collaborated with the Cornell advancement office to analyze gift funds to the college over time and by location and presented the findings to stakeholders in an interpretable manner.

**Introduction to Data Science** *(Three sections)*

- Re-designed existing and created website at: <https://dsc223-fb2-2022.github.io/website/>
- Utilized R within RStudio Server environment; primarily Rmarkdown + tidyverse
- Used an open source book, *Data Science in a Box* by Mine Cetinkaya-Rundel. Available at <https://datasciencebox.org/>
- Development of new data ethics materials in collaboration with Dr. Megan Altman
- Talk about this course, and the course materials are available at <https://bit.ly/3Qq99Qb>
- Topics include learning R (tidyverse), reproducible research (version control with Git/GitHub), data visualizations, data cleaning/wrangling, data ethics, feature engineering, and communicating with data

**Statistical Methods II** *(Two sections)*

- Taught both in face-to-face and online formats
- Technologies utilized included the LMS Moodle, Google Drive, Panopto, Zoom, and Minitab® statistical software
- Topics included multiple linear and logistic regression, multiple testing procedures, ANOVA, and more from *Stat2: Modeling with Regression and Anova*, 2e by Cannon et. al. (2019)

**Student Capstone** *(One section)*

- Mentored student capstone projects in Mathematics, Data Science, and Statistics.
- Course instruction included weekly meetings, as-needed teaching, and giving feedback on students’ written and oral communications on their projects.
- Project areas were broad, including the twin prime conjecture, estimating mask adherence by county, statistical analysis of trail camera trap data, mathematical modeling of basketball league travel schedules, mathematics in media, hyperbolic geometry, identifying risk factors for diabetes in Mexico, identifying important factors for kids considering college, and predicting election outcomes based on campaign spending.

**Advanced Regression** *(Two sections)*

- Developed course
- Course website at: <https://stats-tgeorge.github.io/STA363_AdvReg/>
- Taught in in-person and hybrid formats
- Use live coding in R for instruction
- Technologies include R, RStudio, LMS Moodle, Google Drive, Panopto, and Zoom
- Cover the class of generalized linear models and models within them from “Applied Generalized Linear Models and Multilevel Models in R” by Paul Roback and Julie Legler (2021). This text utilizes current case studies from open-access publications cited in the text for all examples and exercises.

**Time Series Applications** *(Three sections)*

- Developed course
- Course website at: <https://stats-tgeorge.github.io/STA364_TSApps/>
- Taught in in-person and hybrid formats
- Use live coding in R for instruction
- Technologies utilized include the learning management system Moodle, Google Drive, Panopto, and Zoom
- Topics included an introduction to time series, starting with understanding and identifying autocorrelation using a correlogram. Then various models were covered, including SARIMA, regression, and exponential smoothing.
- Primary text: *Forecasting: Principles and Practice* by Hyndman and Athanasopoulos (2025)

### Mentorship

Cornell College, Mount Vernon, Iowa

**Cornell Summer Research Institute (CSRI)** *(Summer 2021 – 2025)*\
Advising students in statistics and data science projects. The program includes faculty-student mentoring, daily meetings where students present their progress, daily journal entries where students reflect on their progress, and the use of Trello for list-making and tracking deliverables. Projects have included: by county estimation of adherence to masking policies, Shiny dashboards on Iowa watershed water composition, time series modeling on Iowa watershed nitrogen levels, building a homework system using learnR, investigating parasitic wasps and fly RNA, visualizing crimes in Minnesota using an R Shiny dashboard, and statistical analysis on chemical composition of historic pottery samples from Iowa.

**Independent Study for Independent Project** *(Mar 2021 – Apr 2021)*\
Advised a student to create detailed and publishable visualizations for their independent research project in ecology using data collected by the Felidae Foundation. Visualizations were created using R programming and included maps with trails, buffer zones, and camera locations, accompanied by text.

**Advisor of Student Groups in MinneMUDAC Data Science Challenge** *(Spring 2021, 2023, 2025)*\
In 2025, students received a second-place finish in the undergraduate division.

**Office of Academic Affairs, under former Provost Dr. Ilene Crawford** *(Summer 2024)*\
Details under an NDA. Data visualization, feature importance, and statistical modeling, with a small sample, with an associated written report. Approximately 40 hours.

### Computer Languages and Programs

- R Programming, including the tidyverse, package development, R Shiny, and Quarto
- Minitab® Statistical Software
- LaTeX
- Microsoft Office Suite – Proficient in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with Publisher
- Familiarity with Microsoft Power BI, Python and SQL
- Familiarity with Statistics Analysis System (SAS), SAS Enterprise Miner, SAS SQL, and SAS Macros
